name: Musical Instrument Museum
unique: A museum where the headphones switch to the music of whatever gallery you stand in, from a Steinway to a Tibetan trumpet, with instruments from every country.
buzz: People plan two hours and stay four; the mechanical instrument gallery and the artist gallery with Prince's and Clapton's instruments are the two stops.

name: Desert Botanical Garden
unique: Fifty thousand desert plants from around the world on 140 acres in Papago Park, with a butterfly pavilion and a trail through a sonoran desert that looks planted but is wild.
buzz: The cactus and succulent collection is the reason gardeners come and the butterfly exhibit runs in spring; summer heat limits the visit to early morning.

name: Heard Museum
unique: The best collection of Native American art in the country, with a room of katsina dolls, contemporary Indigenous painting and a courtyard of pueblo jewelry makers.
buzz: The katsina gallery and the board of trustees' collection are the highlights; the museum is frank about the boarding schools and the jewelry market is real.

name: Saguaro National Park
unique: Two districts of saguaro forest around Tucson, with a scenic loop drive, petroglyphs and trails through cactus that can live 150 years.
buzz: The west district at sunset is the photograph and the east district has the loop drive; go early or late, the midday heat is dangerous.

name: Pima Air and Space Museum
unique: One of the largest aircraft collections in the country, with 400 planes across 80 acres, including a SR-71 and a B-29, plus a tram tour of the bone yard.
buzz: The outdoor storage rows are the reason enthusiasts come and the tram saves walking; the hangars are hot in summer.

name: Mission San Xavier del Bac
unique: The white desert mission on the Tohono O'odham reservation, with painted interior walls, carved doors and a restoration that has lasted decades.
buzz: The interior is the surprise and the fry bread stand outside is the local lunch; it is an active church, so visitors should respect services.

name: Grand Canyon Skywalk
unique: A glass horseshoe suspended 4,000 feet above the Colorado on the Hualapai reservation, reached by a dirt road and a shuttle from the west rim.
buzz: The view is real and the pricing is confusing, with packages for the skywalk, the ranch and the boat; cameras are not allowed on the glass.

name: Oatman
unique: A gold camp on Route 66 where wild burros walk the main street, with a wooden sidewalk, a saloon and a gunfight show for tourists.
buzz: The burros are the reason children love it and the drive over the Black Mountains is the scenic route; the town is tiny and the shows are corny on purpose.

name: London Bridge
unique: The 1831 London Bridge, bought, dismantled stone by stone and rebuilt over a Colorado River canal in the desert, with an English village around it.
buzz: The story is better than the bridge and the boat tour under it is the fun; the lake is the real attraction for most visitors.

name: Yuma Territorial Prison
customer: History people, true crime fans, families
unique: A territorial prison built into a bluff above the Colorado, with cell blocks, a guard tower and the story of the inmates who built the railroad and died in the heat.
buzz: The cell block and the dark cell are the tour and the guides tell the stories well; it is a compact site and the river view is the setting.

name: Kofa National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Six hundred thousand acres of Sonoran desert protecting a herd of desert bighorn sheep, with rugged dirt roads, palm canyons and old mines.
buzz: The sheep are hard to see and that is the point; the roads need high clearance and the summer heat is lethal.

name: Colorado River State Historic Park
unique: The quartermaster depot and the siphon that diverted the Colorado to irrigate the desert, in a park on the river levee.
buzz: The engineering story of the canal is the reason to stop and the buildings are restored; it is small and pairs with the prison.

name: Tumacacori National Historical Park
unique: The adobe ruins of a mission church on the Santa Cruz, with a museum on the O'odham and Yaqui people and a orchard of heirloom fruit trees.
buzz: The church walls and the quiet are the visit and the rangers explain the mission system honestly; the December fiesta is the local tradition.

name: Patagonia Lake State Park
unique: A 265 acre lake in a canyon of the Patagonia Mountains, with a beach, boat rentals and a birding trail where the hummingbird migration passes in summer.
buzz: The lake is the swimming and the birds are the reason naturalists come; the campground books out and the water is cold in spring.

name: Tonto Natural Bridge
unique: A 183 foot tall natural travertine bridge with a creek running under it, and trails down to the water through a cave and along the rim.
buzz: The trail under the bridge is steep and slick and the view from the top is the easy version; the park is small and the parking is limited.

name: Roosevelt Lake
unique: The reservoir formed by the Theodore Roosevelt Dam, the first big federal reclamation project, with a bridge named after the dam and desert mountains all around.
buzz: The lake is the fishing and the dam is the history; the water level varies and the summer heat is brutal.

name: Homolovi State Park
unique: Ancestral Puebloan village sites on the Little Colorado, with pottery sherds on the surface and a campground with a view of the Painted Desert.
buzz: The ruins are unexcavated and the rangers ask you not to pick up the pottery; the park is quiet and the sunset over the mesa is the reason to camp.

name: Fool Hollow Lake
unique: A lake in the White Mountains with a campground under ponderosa pines, a swim beach and a trail around the shore, at 6,300 feet.
buzz: It is the cool summer escape for Phoenix and the campground is the draw; the lake is small and the trout fishing is stocked.

name: Mount Graham
unique: A 10,720 foot sky island above the desert with a road to the top, a spruce fir forest and an observatory where the Vatican runs a telescope.
buzz: The drive from desert to alpine forest in an hour is the experience and the observatory tour needs booking; the mountain is closed to the public in some seasons for the red squirrel.

name: Gila Box Riparian National Conservation Area
unique: Twenty three miles of the Gila and San Simon rivers with cottonwood galleries, beaver and 200 bird species, in a desert canyon.
buzz: The float in spring is the reason to come and the creek trails are quiet; the water is seasonal and the roads are rough.

name: Cibola National Wildlife Refuge
unique: A Colorado River floodplain refuge where sandhill cranes and hundreds of thousands of geese winter, with a driving loop and a walk in aviary.
buzz: The crane season from November to February is the spectacle and the auto loop is easy; summer is empty and very hot.

name: Hi Jolly Monument
customer: Road trippers, history fans, RV snowbirds
unique: A stone pyramid over the grave of Hadji Ali, the Syrian camel driver who ran the army's 1850s camel experiment, in a town of rock shops and winter RVers.
buzz: The camel story is the reason to stop and the January rock and gem show is the other one; the town swells to a million visitors in winter.

name: Morenci Mine Overlook
unique: A viewpoint over one of the largest open pit copper mines in North America, where the pit is miles wide and the haul trucks look like toys.
buzz: The scale is the attraction and the overlook is free; the mine is active so check access and do not enter closed roads.

name: Chiricahua National Monument
unique: A forest of eroded rhyolite hoodoos and balanced rocks in the sky islands, with a loop trail through the columns and a view into the desert.
buzz: The Heart of Rocks loop is the hike and the far park is quiet; the road to the top is steep and the summer monsoon brings lightning.

name: Ramsey Canyon Preserve
unique: A canyon in the Huachuca Mountains where 15 species of hummingbird pass through in summer, with a shaded trail along a creek.
buzz: Hummingbird season from April to September is the reason to come and the feeders at the visitor center are the viewing; reservations are required.

name: Wupatki and Sunset Crater
unique: A lava flow and cinder cone beside a 900 year old pueblo of red sandstone with a ball court and a blowhole, on the same loop road.
buzz: The contrast between the black lava and the red pueblo is the photograph; the Wupatki ruins are quiet and the loop drive is 35 miles.

name: Grand Canyon Railway
unique: A restored train that runs 65 miles from Williams to the South Rim, with a 1920s parlor car, a buffet car and a staged train robbery on the way back.
buzz: The dome car and the wild west show are the family draw; the train arrives at the rim and the return is a long day, so book the class you want.

name: Petrified Forest National Park
unique: A drive through the Painted Desert and fields of petrified wood, with a 225 million year old log jam, petroglyphs and a 1930s inn built of stone.
buzz: The Blue Mesa trail is the walk and the Painted Desert at sunset is the photograph; removing petrified wood is illegal and the park is 50 miles from anywhere.

name: Montezuma Castle
unique: A five story cliff dwelling built into a limestone alcove by the Sinagua, with a path along the creek below and a sycamore grove.
buzz: The dwelling is viewed from below and the scale is the surprise; it is a one hour stop and the Well nearby is included.

name: Jerome
unique: A copper mining town built on a 30 degree slope above the Verde Valley, once called the wickedest town in the west, now galleries, wine bars and a state park.
buzz: The sliding jail and the state park are the history and the view from the upper streets is the photograph; parking is on a steep hill and the town is busy on weekends.
